## Speakers and questions

The moderator supplies introductions, timing and handoffs, without an independent motion case. ## Preserve adopted burdens and qualifications

Giunta presents a two-step case: establish early apostolic appearance proclamations, then compare sincerity and possible explanations. His ordinary historical reliability arguments initially support transmission of the proclamation, not direct observation of resurrection. He calls the Luke/Acts author “Fred” deliberately to avoid assuming authorship. He explicitly qualifies the Acts 2 reconstruction as early preaching rather than proof of Peter’s exact words. His main evidence is the 1 Corinthians 15 creed and Acts 2; he repeatedly distinguishes this from a case requiring Gospel reliability. Evaluate the bridge he actually uses.

Giunta accepts that sincerity does not itself establish truth and that evidence can favor a hypothesis without establishing its conclusion. He invokes background probability, does not simply assume that atheism is irrational, and clarifies in the audience round that a plausible naturalistic alternative would challenge his case without proving what actually happened. He retracts “no value” for a bare resurrection report and later qualifies universal scholar language to teaching professors after counterexamples. Preserve the actual timing of these qualifications; later refinements do not manufacture earlier response duties. His final methodological-naturalism/inerrancy analogy is a substantive closing development and must receive coverage consideration.

Dillahunty distinguishes withholding belief from proving that resurrection never occurred, while positively judging legend probable. Do not assign him a universal disproof burden or treat all his claims as mere withholding. His prior-demonstration requirement for supernatural explanations, critique of historical access to private experiences, tentative legend preference and moral/theological objections carry their own stated burdens. Conditional naturalistic examples in cross-examination are not asserted historical facts. In audience answers he explicitly rejects unsupported drug explanations and says discrepancies alone do not show that no event occurred. His claim that resurrection probability cannot be calculated is distinct from claiming a known zero probability. His later explanation differentiates practical foundational assumptions from an infinite regress of skepticism.

The participants’ outside websites, named scholars and prior conversations are referenced in the source but are not extra evidence the reviewers may fetch. Assess the support actually presented. Do not import unpublished premises or penalize a failure to answer new closing material when no reply opportunity remains. A reply can target an inference rather than affirm a competing historical reconstruction.

Principal limitation: Knowing that God exists does not determine love or submission, as Dillahunty explicitly notes, and conditioning evidence on readiness risks making sincere nonbelief unfalsifiably attributable to a deficient will. Live burden: Giunta must explain why clearer evidence would undermine authentically reciprocal, morally significant freedom and provide a noncircular way to distinguish resistant seekers from willing people who remain unconvinced.

moves.description: Dillahunty closes that layered transmission uncertainty, an unverified supernatural cause, and moral questions about divine sacrifice jointly prevent confidence and weaken the proposed redemptive background.
moves.critique: Strongest feature: The closing integrates historical, methodological, and theological objections into a cumulative case for reasonable doubt, while expressly directing its conclusion against certainty rather than claiming a demonstrated impossibility. Principal limitation: Dillahunty sometimes makes categorical claims about what historical methods can never confirm, compresses complex source transmission into a uniformly degraded chain, and characterizes confident believers’ assurance as compensation without sufficient argumentative support. Live burden: He must keep the evidential case primary and show how particular theological tensions lower Giunta’s background probability without treating disputed accounts of atonement or divine morality as settled.
